content_units: Morocco in 7 Days: Best-Fit Trip Plan

A 2-base itinerary works well for your dates, budget, and pace:   Marrakech + one Sahara-edge desert stay near Merzouga  . This gives you strong architecture and food time in Marrakech, one proper desert experience, and avoids constant repacking.
7-Day Morocco Plan with 2 Hotel Bases
Trip setup
-   Base 1:   Marrakech — 4 nights
-   Base 2:   Merzouga / Erg Chebbi area — 2 nights
-   Final night:   use your 4 Marrakech nights so your last night is still in Marrakech before departure
- This keeps the trip practical while staying within your   2 hotel bases maximum
Day   Base   Plan   Travel Time   Budget Guide
1 — Sat 10 Oct   Marrakech   Arrive, settle into riad, light medina walk, Jemaa el-Fnaa dinner   Minimal   €90
2 — Sun 11 Oct   Marrakech   Bahia Palace, Ben Youssef Madrasa area, souks, rooftop dinner   Minimal   €95
3 — Mon 12 Oct   Marrakech   Jardin Majorelle/YSL area or Saadian/Tin Mal-inspired architecture focus, food tour or cooking class   Minimal   €110
4 — Tue 13 Oct   Merzouga   Private/shared transfer via Atlas and Dades/Todra direction toward desert   9–10 hrs   €170
5 — Wed 14 Oct   Merzouga   Desert day: camel or 4x4 dunes, sunset, camp dinner, music, stars   Light local travel   €160
6 — Thu 15 Oct   Marrakech   Return to Marrakech, relaxed final evening in a comfortable riad   9–10 hrs   €150
7 — Fri 16 Oct   Marrakech   Departure day, short hammam/brunch if timing allows   Minimal   €55
Day 1: Arrive in Marrakech
- Morning/Afternoon: airport arrival, transfer to riad in the medina or near it.
- Afternoon: keep it easy with   Rahba Kedima  , side alleys, and first-look architecture.
- Dinner: start with classic Moroccan dishes like   tanjia, lamb tagine, zaalouk, and pastries   around Jemaa el-Fnaa or a nearby rooftop.
- Good pace note: do not book major sightseeing today; use it to adjust and orient.
Marrakech map
Day 2: Marrakech architecture and old-city detail
- Morning:   Bahia Palace   and nearby mellah lanes.
- Afternoon:   Ben Youssef Madrasa   area, Almoravid/Koutoubia exterior appreciation, artisan souks.
- Food: lunch on   mechoui, harira, or briouats  ; dinner at a modern Moroccan restaurant.
- This is your strongest architecture day without rushing.
Bahia Palace
Day 3: Gardens, design, and food
- Morning:   Jardin Majorelle   and the YSL museum district, or swap in   Saadian Tombs   if you want more historic detail.
- Afternoon: slow café break, then a   food tour or cooking class   for market-to-table experience.
- Dinner: focus on regional flavors rather than tourist set menus.
- This day balances architecture/design with your food interest.
Majorelle
Day 4: Transfer to the desert edge
- Route: Marrakech to   Merzouga / Erg Chebbi   by private transfer or organized small-group circuit.
- Scenic stops: Atlas viewpoints, kasbah landscapes, valley stops.
- Overnight: choose a   comfortable auberge/hotel near dunes  , not a remote camp yet if you want less friction.
- Moderate-pace note: this is a long day, but doing it once each way is better than adding extra hotel stops.
Erg Chebbi
Day 5: Desert experience
- Morning: slow breakfast and rest.
- Afternoon:   camel ride or 4x4 dune excursion  .
- Sunset: dunes at golden hour.
- Evening:   camp-style dinner, music, and stargazing  .
- Best fit for your trip: book   one quality desert experience   rather than trying to add extra towns.
Best fit for your trip: book   one quality desert experience   rather than trying to add extra towns, Morocco
Desert planning
Day 6: Return to Marrakech
- Travel back to Marrakech.
- Check into the same riad if possible for simplicity.
- Final evening: hammam, quiet courtyard dinner, or one last souk walk for ceramics/spices/textiles.
- This protects your departure day from transport risk.
Marrakech airport
Day 7: Departure
- If your flight is later: relaxed breakfast, quick hammam, or last pastry/coffee stop.
- Keep airport transfer buffer generous from the medina.
Budget Split for €900 Excluding Flights
A realistic target is   about €820–€900 total  , depending on whether you use shared or private desert transport.
-   Hotels/riads:   €300–€380
- Marrakech riad: about   €60–€85/night x 4
- Desert-side hotel/camp equivalent: about   €70–€110/night x 2
-   Desert transport + excursion:   €220–€320
- Shared small-group option keeps you closer to budget
- Private transfer adds comfort but pushes total up
- Roughly   €20–€27/day
- One nicer dinner and one food activity fit comfortably
-   Sightseeing/entry fees:   €40–€70
-   Local taxis / airport transfers / tips:   €50–€80
-   Contingency/shopping cushion:   €50–€80
Best budget fit
- Stay in a   mid-range riad   in Marrakech rather than luxury.
- Use a   shared desert trip with upgraded lodging   instead of fully private transport.
- Spend a little more on   food and one memorable desert night  , a little less on constant moving.
Main Tradeoffs to Expect
Option tradeoffs that matter most
Option 1:   Marrakech + Merzouga     Best match for desert + architecture + moderate pace   Long overland travel days
Route map
Option 2:   Marrakech only + Agafay desert     Much easier logistics and more city time   Desert is less iconic than Sahara dunes
Agafay area
Option 3:   Marrakech + Essaouira     Excellent food/coastal atmosphere and gentler pace   No true desert experience
Essaouira map
Recommended choice
-   Best overall for your priorities:     Marrakech + Merzouga
- Why: it gives you the   strongest architecture base  ,   great food opportunities  , and   one real desert experience  , while still limiting hotel changes.
- Biggest compromise: two long transfer days reduce sightseeing time.
Practical Notes for These Dates
Planning context
- Mid-October is generally a very good window: warm in Marrakech, more comfortable in the desert than peak summer.
- I assumed your flight arrives early enough on   10 Oct   to use that as a real first day, and departs on   16 Oct   from Marrakech.
- I also assumed your   €900 excludes flights   but includes hotels, transport, food, and normal sightseeing.
